tool: VCFcache, branch feature/fused-routing at c878d86c3, engines legacy and fused
engine_binary: vcfcache-engine 0.1.0, prebuilt locally and copied (cluster glibc 2.43 matches; HTSlib statically linked; no cargo on the cluster)
deployment: /results/deployment/vcfcache-fused-c878d86c, shadowed over the stale editable install via PYTHONPATH. `vcfcache --version` reports 0.5.3 from the old dist-info; both jobs assert the branch by requiring --engine in the CLI.
level: engine/overhead profiling; Arm A and the span sweep invoke no annotator at all
invocation: vcfcache annotate -a <cache> --engine {legacy,fused} --stats-dir <dir>; one untimed warm-up then 3 timed reps per cell
assays: real ACMG SF v3.3 panel and Twist core exome samples

result.legacy_span_dependence: flat 19.6-21.3 s from 1 to 22 contigs: a full-cache pass, unrestricted
result.region_restriction_win: 2x at 2-4 contigs (10.2 s vs 19.5 s legacy), and that is what WHOLE-CONTIG restriction buys: route uses -r <contig>, so a few-gene panel still reads all of that contig's cache
result.panel_split: legacy 27.0 s total = 23.7 s VCFcache + 3.3 s VEP (3 misses of 203)
result.wes_split: legacy 156.3 s total = 27.0 s VCFcache + 129.3 s VEP (1,339 misses of 75,135)

note: Answers where the campaign's panel loss comes from: VCFcache's fixed term, not annotator start-up and not per-variant work. Legacy's fixed term is ~20-24 s and flat across contig span, because legacy applies no region restriction. Whole-contig restriction in fused route is ~2x faster than legacy at 2-4 contigs. Fused is slower than legacy at 1 contig and at 22 contigs and must not be promoted to default on this evidence. See ANALYSIS.md: five claims in the first version were too strong and are corrected there, with the experiment that would settle the remaining mechanism question.

excluded.1253_arm_C: all three inputs were single-contig whatever span they claimed; the genome-wide pool is contig-ordered and selection took the first 250 matching rows. Superseded by job 1254. Rows left in the raw TSV.

superseded_attempts.1252: died silently on `awk {exit}` SIGPIPEing bcftools under `set -o pipefail`; proven in isolation (rc=141 vs rc=0). Fixed by draining; the 3.1 Gb cache scan also replaced with 22 indexed windows.

caveats.mechanism_not_established: The 22-contig per-worker spread (9.9/21.3/32.6/45.6 s) has three live candidates this run cannot separate: grouping balances bcftools index --stats of the INPUT (variant counts) not cache records; repeated cache-prefix traversal, which the near-arithmetic progression fits; and uncontrolled threading. An earlier version called it 'purely scheduling', which is withdrawn.
caveats.single_contig_explained: workers is clamped to the contig count, so 1 contig gives workers==1, that branch sets contigs=[None], and route then builds selection=''. With one worker there is NO -r restriction, so it streams the whole 18.87 M-record cache. A code path, not a scheduling artefact.
caveats.threading_uncontrolled: Legacy overlay passes --threads {threads} (workflow_manager.py:395-403); the bcftools annotate inside fused route passes no thread option, and compression_threads = 8//4-2 = 0. Part of the legacy/fused gap may be threading; an isolated comparison is required.
caveats.worker_count: 8 CPUs configured on 16-vCPU nodes gives cpu_budget//2 = 4 workers. The previously stated '~14 s over 8 workers' is withdrawn as an extrapolation at a worker count never run.
caveats.vep_column_is_a_residual: The VEP figures are real-input total minus the matched zero-miss cell, so they absorb input-format, composition, indexing and normalization differences too. They are this cache's VEP 115.2 --everything recipe and cannot establish the fastVEP campaign's breakdown.
caveats.slopes_exploratory: 45.1 and 26.8 us/variant come from two points, three reps, one node. Exploratory only; not new per-variant constants beside the production 27.5 us.
caveats.hit_rates_not_cohort_results: 98.2-98.5% here is 1000 Genomes against a gnomAD AF>=1% cache, not held out. Overhead is hit-rate independent so the profiling stands, but these must not be quoted as coverage.
